messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] PAGER -> multi-gpu collective failure detected on cluster-prod-east. severity: P1. job_id=run-5243. error="NCCL_COLLECTIVE_TIMEOUT + CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS". affected nodes: node-az2-gpu-07,node-az2-gpu-08,node-az2-gpu-09,node-az2-gpu-10. ts=2026-03-15T02:12:25Z

sre-jamie: ack, joining. pulling logs and metrics now.

eng-maya: i'm eng-runtime oncall, i'll take this. quick ask: customer impact? which jobs failed?

customer-success-ash: two active customers hit job failures. CS-4872 is open. one retried and succeeded with smaller batch, other is still queued and flagged as high priority. letting them know we're investigating.

ml-ivan: context from model team: the training is pipeline-parallel (8 shards). a change to KV cache retention was merged yesterday (retention segments 6->12). suspicious that KV growth plus larger micro-batches pushed a codepath we haven't exercised.

infra-lin: infra sees GPU mem spike to ~100% on node-07, then container logs show `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` and subsequent NCCL aborts. kernel logs show GPU reset on node-07.

sre-jamie: logs snippet from rank 3 (node-az2-gpu-09):

```
[2026-03-15T02:12:24Z] [rank 3] NCCL INFO comm 0x7f8b1c2d: Allreduce failed: ncclCommAbort
[2026-03-15T02:12:24Z] [rank 3] CUDA ERROR at kernel launch: an illegal memory access was encountered
[2026-03-15T02:12:24Z] [rank 3] aborting collective: ncclAllReduce
[2026-03-15T02:12:24Z] [container] stacktrace: ...
```

eng-maya: immediate mitigations we can run now (low-risk):
1) cordon + drain node-az2-gpu-07 to stop scheduling onto noisy hardware.
2) restart container runtime on node-08 and 09 to clear any lingering GPU state.
3) reduce micro-batch on active jobs (reduce OOM pressure).
4) set `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` for canary pool to get more telemetry.
5) trigger fallback to single-gpu model variant for customer interactive jobs if still failing.

infra-lin: executing 1 & 2 now.

```
kubectl cordon node-az2-gpu-07
kubectl drain node-az2-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n prod
ssh node-az2-gpu-08 'sudo systemctl restart containerd'
```

oncall-bot: automated action -> autoscaler reduced concurrent training slots in pool-prod by 30%. fallback routing enabled for heavy jobs.

ml-ivan: suggestion: check for shard alignment mismatch — i've seen `illegal memory access` from misaligned tensor-split + collective pattern when KV memory grows unexpectedly. run `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` on nodes and search dmesg for GPU Xid codes.

sre-jamie: did `kubectl drain` on node-07 complete. restarted runtime on node-08. rebalanced 3 pods off node-07. errors per-minute dropped from 12 -> 1 on the affected job group.

customer-success-ash: sent customer update: "we identified multi-GPU collective failures related to GPU memory pressure; mitigation in progress; ETA ~30m for restart/relief."

eng-maya: applying a hotpatch to canary: force KV retention back to 6 for canary model instances and set `NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0` to avoid collnet paths.

```
kubectl set env deploy/model-svc CANARY=true MODEL_KV_RETENTION=6 NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0 -n prod-canary
kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-svc -n prod-canary
```

ml-ivan: running reproducer on staging with the same shard/batch config. if we can reproduce, will push a deterministic fix. also capturing `nvprof` traces for the kernel before we revert.

sre-jamie: turned on `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` for canary pool and collected NCCL logs; also saved dmesg from node-07 (attached to internal incident record). journal shows `NVRM: GPU Xid 31` resets shortly before illegal memory access. driver version on node-07 is 546.XX; checking for recent kernel/driver mismatch.

infra-lin: found pending driver package on node-07 from previous maintenance that didn't apply properly. applying unified driver rollout to match cluster baseline. will patch node-07 in maintenance window after draining.

eng-maya: handoff plan — handing to night SRE in ~15m. checklist i'm leaving:
- node-az2-gpu-07 cordoned and drained (done)
- container runtime restarted on node-08 (done)
- canary env patched MODEL_KV_RETENTION=6 (done)
- NCCL debug logs captured (done)
- customer updates issued (CS-4872 updated)
- postmortem owner assigned (ml-ivan)

oncall-bot: handoff scheduled to @sre-lee at +15m. bridge created: #inc-3725012345-bridge.

sre-jamie: SLO impact so far: spike in job-failure rate from baseline 0.2% -> 4.1% for 18 minutes. approx 0.8% of total cluster throughput affected. recorded for postmortem.

customer-success-ash: will keep both customers informed; marking CS-4872 as "monitoring" until we confirm long-term remediation.

ml-ivan: assigning postmortem id PM-172 to myself. suspected root cause: KV cache retention change + edge-case driver/kernel state -> illegal memory write during NCCL allreduce across pipeline shards. will include timeline, mitigations, and a rollback/validation checklist.

eng-maya: thanks everyone. i'll follow up with the full incident body and add recommended guardrails (preflight for KV retention changes, canary memory stress tests). :thumbsup: will update the thread with any new findings in the next 30m.
